correctness.rationale: Expanding R on the basis e,f with [e,f]=f gives precisely b(ad−a−bc−d)=0 and d²(a−1)−bc(d+1)=0; bilinearity makes the four basis pairs exhaustive, two identically zero, and the other two negatives. For b=0, branches (d=0) and (a=1,d≠0) exhaust all possibilities; for b≠0, substitution forces a+d=0 and bc=−a² over any characteristic, including 2. Disjoint sizes q²,q(q−1),q(q−1) give N=3q²−2q and rank counts (1,2q²−q−1,q(q−1)); invertibles exactly a=1,b=0,d≠0. Independent direct matrix and bracket enumeration for q=2,3,5,7 gives (1,5,2),(1,14,6),(1,44,20),(1,90,42). Repeating over F_{q^m} yields N_m=3q^{2m}−2q^m, hence zeta (1−qT)^2/(1−q²T)^3 for the REDUCED solution locus only. No claim of scheme reducedness.
